youtube.baslik: Which test values define bilateral vestibular loss? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: Under the 2017 Barany Society criteria, laboratory evidence of bilateral vestibulopathy needs only one of three tests: horizontal video head impulse gain below 0.6 on both sides, a summed warm and cold caloric response below 6 degrees per second on each side, or very low gain with clearly increased phase lead on rotary chair testing. Normal lateral canal gain is usually above about 0.8. If all caloric responses are small, a technical problem is ruled out first.

cumleler: Which test values define bilateral vestibular loss?
For bilateral vestibulopathy, one of three tests can provide laboratory evidence.
Video head impulse gain is below 0.6 on both sides.
Or each side's summed caloric response is below six degrees per second.
Or rotary chair gain is very low, with clearly increased phase lead.
Normally, lateral canal gain is above about 0.8.
